Research Note Sep 30, 2026 360° ReconstructionVisual-InertialMetric Scale

Can a 360° Camera Measure Its Own Scale?

Metric Scale for Insta360 Reconstructions from the Camera's Embedded IMU, Validated Against a Co-Mounted LiDAR

OVER Research

The 1 kHz IMU inside an Insta360 X5 gives our 360° reconstructions metric scale to 0.81% against a co-mounted LiDAR, 2.4× closer than the phone it replaced. On the way we found that the textbook visual-inertial alignment, solved over a whole survey, overestimates scale by 3.4% with a consistent sign; solving each contiguous run on its own and averaging removes the bias. On fifty production surveys (33 km) the public estimator ran unattended, passed its own checks every time and agreed with the phone to σ = 2.3%.

Research Note Aug 28, 2026 Gaussian SplattingEmbodied AIVision-Language Models

A VLM Inside a 3D Capture Follows the Coordinate, Not the Room

Driving a Vision-Language Model Through a Gaussian-Splat Reconstruction, and Measuring How Much of It Is Vision

OVER Research

We put a robot pose inside a Gaussian-splat capture, rendered its view live at every step and let a vision-language model choose one action per frame. It works as a loop and produces a measured arrival — 19 steps, 1.03 m inside a 1.20 m radius, scored geometrically rather than self-reported — and a more useful negative result: a trivial compass follower reproduces 35–71% of the agent's actions, and if the goal's direction is withheld it never approaches the target, so this is coordinate-following with a visual veto rather than vision-and-language navigation. Two findings come with it: a harness that phrases privileged information as an instruction stops measuring the model, and a goal is only scorable if the capture walked inside its success radius (one of ours contained none of 438 capture poses). Pointed the other way, the same walk could hunt the poses a capture barely saw and hand them to a generative filler — stated at the end as a direction, deliberately not evidenced here.

Research Note Jul 31, 2026 360° ReconstructionLIDARBenchmark

How Accurate Is Our Automatic 360°-Camera Reconstruction Pipeline?

Benchmarking the OVR 360° Pipeline Against a Simultaneous LIDAR Survey of the Same Site

OVER Research

We rode a LIDAR scanner and our 360° camera on the same pole through a 40 × 25 m site and compared the two reconstructions point by point: median surface agreement of 3.9 cm — at the reference scanner's own declared accuracy — drift-free geometry over the 118 m path, and one uniform 2.9% scale disagreement that the measurement chain traces to the metric reference rather than the reconstruction, removable with a single scalar.

Research Note Jul 31, 2026 LGMMachine PerceptionFine-Tuning

Can 1,000 Open Scenes Make a State-of-the-Art 3D Model Better?

Assessing the OVER Dataset by Fine-Tuning a 3D Foundation Model on Its Open Sample

OVER Research

An empirical assessment of the OVER dataset for research, run entirely on OverMaps-1k — the open 1,000-scene sample anyone can download from Hugging Face: pose accuracy improves visibly on our domain, catastrophic forgetting is measured and defused through WiSE weight merging, and a scaling analysis shows how much data the gain requires.
